explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/980: for k ≥ 2, is Σ_{p<x} n_k(p) ~ c_k x/log x for some c_k > 0, with n_k(p) the least k-th power nonresidue mod p? Proved by Elliott. leastNonresidue is the least n > 0 that is not a k-th power in ZMod p. residueSum k x sums it over the primes p < x with p ≡ 1 (mod k), following Elliott's setting as the docstring says. This choice avoids primes where every residue is a k-th power, and it only affects the constant. The statement asks for c > 0 with residueSum ~ c·x/log x. Faithful.
